title: Attorney General of Nebraska

context.text: Both nominees were unopposed in the May 12, 2026 primaries: Republican incumbent Mike Hilgers received 161,220 votes and Democrat Jocelyn Brasher 111,939.
In 2022 Hilgers won the open seat with 69.7% against Larry Bolinger of the Legal Marijuana Now Party.
Brasher worked for five years as an assistant attorney general in the office Hilgers now leads, including about nine months under Hilgers.
The Nebraska Secretary of State's list of Nov. 3, 2026 statewide contests shows two candidates for Attorney General: Mike Hilgers (Republican) and Jocelyn Brasher (Democratic).

candidates.name: Mike Hilgers
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the May 12, 2026 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists: fight federal overreach, protect the Constitution, protect children, stand with law enforcement, defend innocent life, and keep communities safe.
Says he has focused on protecting minors and defending parental rights, cracking down on scammers to protect consumers, and securing serious criminal convictions.

record.text: Announced a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging it deceived Nebraskans about the safety of ChatGPT for minors, under the Nebraska Consumer Protection Act, the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act and the Age-Appropriate Online Design Code Act.
Filed suit against TP-Link as part of his office's litigation over the company's ties to China.
Filed an amicus brief in the U.S. Supreme Court in support of parents' religious rights.

His office accused petitioners of fraud in the successful 2024 ballot initiative that legalized medical cannabis in Nebraska, and is part of a multistate lawsuit seeking to stop the federal reclassification of marijuana, according to the Nebraska Examiner.

candidates.name: Jocelyn Brasher
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the May 12, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Names consumer protection, public safety and health care as her top priorities.
Says she would assemble a task force to combat crimes against children and, on her first day, work to provide guidance for patient access to medical cannabis.
Campaign site lists: protect consumers, strengthen public safety, respect Nebraska voters, and restore public trust and accountability.

statements.quote: work to ensure immigration enforcement in Nebraska complies with constitutional requirements and due process
statements.context: Reported by the Nebraska Examiner on her priorities if elected
